ogTitle: Chale Wote: Accra’s street art festival
subtitle: Accra’s streets become a gallery
answer: Chale Wote is a street art festival in Accra, run by the arts collective Accra [dot] Alt since 2011. Usually over about a week in August, it fills the streets of James Town and, more recently, Osu with murals, graffiti, performance, music, film, installations and street boxing. It is free and open to everyone.

sticky.title: August in Accra
sticky.text: It’s free and runs over several days. Come in the afternoon and stay late.

sections.title: What Chale Wote is
sections.html: Chale Wote began in 2011, organised by Accra [dot] Alt. Its name is Ga for “friend, let’s go”, and also the name of the everyday flip-flop.[[1]] The early editions ran along High Street in James Town; since then it has spread to venues and neighbourhoods across the city, and the 2023 edition was in Osu.[[1]]

sections.title: What happens
sections.html: Expect street painting and murals, photography, theatre, spoken word, installations, live music and performance, film screenings, street boxing and a procession of cultures.[[1]] Each edition has its own theme: in 2025 it ran from 19 to 24 August under the theme “The Orbs Beneath the Nile Lead to Kongo”.[[2]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: check the year’s programme: James Town and Osu are the usual hubs, a short ride apart.
When: afternoons and evenings are busiest. It’s hot, so carry water and wear comfortable shoes.
Photos: artists and performers usually welcome cameras, but ask before close-ups of people.
Also in August: Homowo is celebrated in James Town in the same month.

faq.a: A free street art festival in Accra, held each year since 2011, with murals, performance, music, film and more.

faq.q: When is the Chale Wote festival?
faq.a: Usually in August, over about a week. In 2025 it ran from 19 to 24 August.
It is Ga for “friend, let’s go”, and also the name of the everyday flip-flop.
